From seeing to doing

More than a
phone connection.

Turn your phone's visible interface into tools your AI can understand and use. Keep the assistant you already know.

◎

See what's on screen

Read accessible controls and text, or take a screenshot. When an App exposes no controls, your assistant can still use the visible screen.

01
↗

Take the next step

Tap, long-press, swipe, enter text and open allowed Apps. Check the screen again after each action.

02
⏸

More devices. One control queue.

Connect several phones and computers. AI clients request control and take turns; your phone shows who is active and who is waiting.

03
↓

Send files to your phone

Send from the desktop window or your AI. Accept on the phone, then share to WeChat, WhatsApp or another App. You choose the recipient. Up to 50 MiB per file.

04
✓

Your access, screen and activity

Select all allowed Apps, uncheck any you do not need, then save. Keep the screen awake during control and view a timeline of actions in Settings.

05

AI mobile testing

Use the phone like a user.
Let AI run your tests.

Let the AI on your computer read screens, tap, type and swipe on a real phone to check the flows you are building.

⌘

Test as you develop

After changing a screen, ask your AI to open the App, use its buttons and fill in forms. Check whether the interface and interactions match your expectations.

↻

Let AI run regression checks

Give your AI the test steps and expected results. Let it repeat the flow on a real phone and check that existing features still work after an update.

☷

Trace a bug through real actions

Ask your AI to reproduce a flow across screens. Use screenshots, screen state and operation history to find the failing step, then verify the fix.

You set the test goals; your AI operates the phone through PhoneBridge. See the supported features and real-device test results.

Get started

Pair once.
Add your phone to the flow.

You need an Android 11+ phone,
a Windows PC or Mac, and an AI client that supports MCP.

1

Install on your phone

Download the ARM64 APK and enable PhoneBridge's accessibility service in Android settings. For future updates, open About in the App.

Download the App ↗
2

Start on your computer

Open the Windows or macOS client. It starts the service, selects your network and shows the pairing code. No Node.js installation needed.

Choose your desktop download ↓
3

Pair your AI with your phone

Use the same Wi-Fi, tap Scan on your phone and choose allowed Apps. Enable Allow actions when you need taps or typing, then add MCP to your AI client.

Configure MCP ↗
Let your AI help with setup

What to expect

Your phone.
Your choice.

PhoneBridge includes no AI model, cloud relay or telemetry. Your phone connects to a local Hub. How your AI client processes the screen content depends on its model provider and settings.

Does USB need to stay connected?

No. Your phone and computer can connect over the local network. The App's accessibility service takes screenshots and performs actions. You only need to enable accessibility yourself the first time.

Can I connect from another network?

Your phone needs a route to the running computer Hub, for example through a private network or a trusted WSS endpoint. Keep the computer on and the phone unlocked. The connection tested on a real phone so far is over the local network; cross-network access has not been tested yet.

Can it control every App completely?

It cannot bypass the lock screen, fingerprint prompts, protected screenshots or an App's own restrictions. It operates on allowed Apps' visible interfaces and does not read their private databases.

Who is this ready for?

Windows and macOS clients include their runtime. Mac packages support Apple Silicon and Intel on macOS 13+; the preview is not Apple-notarized. You need an AI client that supports MCP. The APK uses a preview debug signer; behavior may vary across phones and Android versions. The repository documents the actual test coverage.

Can I modify and host it myself?

Yes. PhoneBridge is MIT licensed. The Flutter + Kotlin App and Node.js bridge are on GitHub. Issues and improvements are welcome.
